findings.title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() breaks compilation
findings.body: `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only method added in the superclass `UsernamePasswordForm` is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, and no no-arg overload exists anywhere in the hierarchy. The services module will not compile, so neither the fix nor the new tests can run. The call should pass the current user, e.g. `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`.

findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, disabling passkeys on normal login and enabling them for every re-auth
findings.body:
The new helper returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. Before this PR, the conditional UI was filled only when no user was selected yet (the normal identity-first login). It is used in `authenticate()` (line 115) and in `challenge(context, error, field)` (line 137), and with this condition:
(1) On a fresh login where `context.getUser()` is null, `fillContextForm` is never called. The webauthn challenge and conditional UI are no longer rendered, so passkey login is broken for all first-time and logged-out logins.
(2) During re-authentication it returns true for any identified user, so the passkey UI is shown even to users with no passkey credential.
The intended condition is `user == null || user.credentialManager().isConfiguredFor(webauthnAuth.getCredentialType())`.

findings.title: Re-auth test for user without passkey disables passkeys realm-wide, so the per-user check is never tested
findings.body:
`reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` sets `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)` for the whole realm. The webauthn form is therefore absent simply because the feature is off, not because the user lacks a passkey. Yet the inline comment at line 304 says passkeys are unavailable "as this user does not have passkey".

The important case is never exercised: passkeys enabled in the realm, and a user without a passkey credential re-authenticating with prompt=login. That case is exactly where the `user != null` logic in `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` misbehaves. The test should keep passkeys enabled and assert the webauthn form is absent for test-user@localhost.
